notes: Direct HTTP fetch worked throughout, no blocks, no robots.txt (404). The site's main nav has a genuine 'NEW ARRIVALS' mega-menu section (distinct from the sibling 'FEATURED' section in the same 'New & Featured' dropdown) with a rollup link ('All New' -> /Products/Feature/All?sub=New) plus 9 real type-filtered children (New Ceiling, New Wall, New Table Lamps, New Floor Lamps, New Outdoor, New Textiles, New Furnishings, New Decor, New Hardware), each its own URL using the site's tag-based ?sub=New query param on the same first-party ASP.NET MVC catalog engine verified in the prior Home-Decor pass (total-product-count span cross-verified against the hidden TotalObjectCount pagination field on every page, all matching exactly). All pages confirmed genuine PLPs on inspection: real product grids, filters, sort, and pagination (banner headings read 'New', 'Ceiling', 'Wall', 'Table Lamp', 'Floor Lamp', 'Exterior', 'New Textiles', 'New Furniture', 'New Decor', 'New Hardware' respectively) -- not marketing/editorial pages. Kept 'All New' as the parent/group row (the site-level rollup of everything newly added) with the 9 type-filtered pages as genuine children, same shape as the shared engine's grouping rules. The 9 children's counts sum to 1805, which is higher than the 1680-count parent rollup -- this is expected cross-listing (a single new product can appear under both a type filter like 'New Wall' and a supercategory filter like 'New Decor'), the same pattern already documented for this company's regular category tree in the prior pass; not treated as an error or duplicate. Per this project's scope (whole-site merchandising PLPs, not restricted to the Home-Decor category boundary used in the earlier project), children spanning Furniture/Textiles/Hardware were kept since they are genuine site-defined New-Arrivals sub-structure, not out-of-scope content invented by us. No separate/aliased New Arrivals URL was found elsewhere in nav, footer, or homepage (the homepage's 'New & Trending' section is a marketing carousel of brand-launch cards, not a PLP, and was not counted).
